findings.title: PAA snippet fields have no length cap — larger injection surface than AIO by file-level contract
findings.suggested_fix: Add .slice(0, 500) on question and .slice(0, 1000) on snippet inside extractPaaEntries (lines 67-68), matching the title/description caps at lines 215-216. Also cap paa.items to 5 entries.
findings.why_it_matters: AIO text is explicitly capped at 4KB to reduce LLM prompt injection surface. PAA entries have no cap and are duplicated into metadata.paa_entries on every organic row (up to 10 rows per task), making the PAA path a larger uncapped injection surface than the guarded AIO field.
evidence: extractPaaEntries lines 65-70: paa.items.map with String(e.title) and String(e.expanded_element?.[0]?.description) — no .slice() applied
paaEntries is attached to metadata.paa_entries on every organic item at line 236, not once per task
AIO cap at line 54: text.slice(0, 4096) with explicit comment 'reduces LLM prompt injection surface from attacker-controlled SERP content'
PAA: 8 entries × 800 chars each × 10 organic rows = 64KB uncapped per task vs 4KB AIO cap
Attacker controls PAA content via their website's People Also Ask appearance; content flows directly to LLM prompt

findings.title: Positional task-ID assignment assumes API response order matches submission order
findings.suggested_fix: Parse taskInfo.tag (set at line 155 as keyword|country|language) to reverse-lookup the original query object, rather than relying on taskList[i] == chunk[i] positional alignment.
findings.why_it_matters: If DataForSEO reorders or omits entries in the POST response (e.g. partial success), the wrong keyword/country/language is permanently associated with a task ID. All organic events from that task carry wrong coordinates, silently corrupting AIO-survival scoring.
evidence: Line 155: task.tag set to keyword|country|language — contains all correlation data but is never used for reverse-lookup
Lines 161-165: taskIdToQuery.set(taskInfo.id, chunk[i]) assumes position i in response equals position i in request
DataForSEO API documentation does not guarantee response-order == submission-order
Partial success responses (some tasks queued, some rejected inline) shift array indices, silently misaligning all subsequent entries

findings.title: retrieved.add outside try permanently drops tasks on transient fetch errors — no retry possible
findings.suggested_fix: Move retrieved.add(taskId) inside the try block after event extraction succeeds. On catch, do not add to retrieved — allow the next poll iteration to retry the task.
findings.why_it_matters: A transient 500 or network error on googleOrganicTaskGetAdvanced causes the task to be permanently counted as done with zero events emitted. The poll loop advances toward totalTasks and exits normally; the SERP event corpus is silently incomplete with no error signal.
evidence: Lines 242-245: catch block executes console.error only, does not rethrow
Line 247: retrieved.add(taskId) runs unconditionally in the outer for-loop body, after the catch block exits
If googleOrganicTaskGetAdvanced throws for every task in a poll round, retrieved.size still increments to totalTasks and loop exits normally with events=[]
No retry mechanism exists; task IDs are not re-queued on error

findings.title: Cascade: partial chunk POST leaves orphaned DataForSEO tasks — next run double-bills for same queries
findings.suggested_fix: Collect the set of successfully-posted task IDs before the poll loop. If the POST for-loop throws mid-way, surface the partial task set in the error response so an operator can cancel or poll them separately.
findings.why_it_matters: DataForSEO charges per task submitted regardless of whether results are ever fetched. Orphaned tasks from failed chunks remain in the account queue. The next daily refresh re-posts the same queries generating new task IDs, incurring double spend. At worst, stale tasks from prior restarts bleed into a future run's tasks_ready queue.
evidence: Lines 147-167: sequential for-loop over chunks; if chunk[N].googleOrganicTaskPost throws, the exception propagates out of runSerpByoConnector
runSafely in ingest_byo.ts catches the throw and returns status=error with events=[] — no partial task cleanup
Chunks 0..N-1 tasks were already submitted to DataForSEO and billed before the throw

tasks_ready guard at line 189 (!taskIdToQuery.has(taskId)) correctly rejects unknown IDs, but only within the same process instance — a restarted process has an empty taskIdToQuery and cannot identify orphaned tasks

findings.title: Composition: COST_PER_CALL sentinel of 0 makes spendStore budget guard permanently dead code for SERP
findings.suggested_fix: After the run, record SerpConnectorResult.estimated_spend_usd (or a conservative per-run estimate) via deps.spendStore.record instead of 0. The current record(connector, 0) means getSpent always returns 0 and the budget guard condition budgetUsd - 0 > 0 is always true.
findings.why_it_matters: The documented intent is to enforce DATAFORSEO_DAILY_BUDGET_USD. The spendStore outer guard in runWithSpend checks budgetUsd - spentUsd <= 0. Because 0 is recorded every run, spentUsd never accumulates, so the guard never fires. The inner guard in runSerpByoConnector also omits spentUsd. Both budget checks are statically fixed — no run-count-based enforcement exists despite the budget infrastructure being wired up.
evidence: ingest_byo.ts line 16: dataforseo_serp_byo: 0 (comment acknowledges it is a sentinel)
Line 126: deps.spendStore.record(connector, COST_PER_CALL[connector] ?? 0.01) — passes 0 for SERP
byo_guard.ts line 58: if (budgetUsd - (spentUsd ?? 0) <= 0) — with spentUsd always 0, condition is never true
dataforseo_serp_byo.ts lines 83-88: inner evaluateByoGuard call omits spentUsd entirely — both guards are static

residual_risks: AIO .slice(0,4096) truncates JavaScript string characters, not Unicode code points. A surrogate pair split at position 4095 produces a lone surrogate in the metadata string; behavior across JSON serializers and LLM tokenizers is inconsistent across runtimes.

googleOrganicTasksReady() is account-global, not scoped to the current run. Process restart mid-poll (after POST, before poll completes) permanently orphans tasks — they reappear in a future run's tasks_ready but are filtered by !taskIdToQuery.has(taskId) and silently discarded without cancellation via DataForSEO task-cancel API.

buildSerpQueries produces a Cartesian product of locationMap entries x keywords. Results are silently truncated to DATAFORSEO_MAX_BATCH_PER_RUN (default 500) at live_read_model.ts line 660 with no caller notification that coverage was dropped.

estimatedSpendUsd (dataforseo_serp_byo.ts line 98) computed from inputs.length before locale filtering and before batch cap — can significantly overstate actual spend, making R17 informational telemetry inaccurate for observability dashboards.
testing_gaps: No test covers extractPaaEntries with long description strings or many entries to assert absence of length caps.
No test for partial chunk POST failure (first chunk succeeds, second throws) verifying orphaned task behavior and double-spend scenario.
No test verifies that retrieved.add fires on googleOrganicTaskGetAdvanced throw — the silent permanent-drop scenario is untested.
No test verifies that COST_PER_CALL=0 results in spendStore never accumulating across repeated runs and that the budget guard never fires for the SERP connector.
